record.original_question: Can one give a rigorous and explicit mathematical solution of the diffraction problem for waves passing through two finite slits in the plane, the setting underlying Young's double-slit experiment in optics and the analogous double-slit experiment in quantum mechanics?

evidence.quote: However the rigorous solution of the problem of diffraction from two slits remains open. This problem is of great mathematical and physical importance, describing as it does Young's famous double slit experiment in optics, and the double slit experiment in quantum mechanics.

artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that while the single-slit/half-plane diffraction problem has classical rigorous solutions (Sommerfeld), the two-slit case is typically treated via approximations (Kirchhoff, Fraunhofer/Fresnel, Rayleigh–Sommerfeld integrals) rather than an exact closed-form solution. No source found provides a rigorous, explicit closed-form solution to the two-slit Helmholtz diffraction problem with edge conditions, consistent with the problem being still open.

status_evidence.title: Diffraction from slits - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The diffraction pattern of two slits of width a separated by distance d is the interference pattern of two point sources... multiplied by the diffraction pattern of a slit of width a.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatments rely on approximations rather than an exact rigorous solution.

status_evidence.title: Fraunhofer diffraction equation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Helmholtz and Kirchhoff developed integral equations for diffraction... and approximations needed to apply them.
status_evidence.claim: Available approaches use Kirchhoff approximations, not an exact rigorous solution for two slits.
